summary: Retracted the monotonicity error: forced equality does NOT carry up in k; NON-forcing carries up, because a k-colouring separating a pair is also a (k+1)-colouring. Sharp corollary proved: if G is (k-1)-colourable then no distinct pair is forced equal at k (recolour one endpoint with the spare colour). Hence a 4-colourable seed can never exhibit a k=5 forced pair, which is why the seed had to contain the 5-chromatic H. Built U = induced unit-distance graph on H union (H+tau), tau=(3/2,sqrt3/2), |tau|^2=3 exactly, in Q(sqrt3,sqrt5,sqrt11) with exact dedup. Results: 1106 points -> 1048 after dedup, overlap 58 (A-only 495, B-only 495), edges 2722 internal A + 2722 internal B + 184 NEW cross edges = 5487 total; overlap is NOT a clique and there are 184 cross edges, so Theorem A does not apply - this is not a clique-sum. chi >= 5 because H is an induced subgraph (inner A edges exactly 2722) and H is 4-UNSAT; chi <= 5 by an explicit 5-colouring re-verified with 0 monochromatic of 5487. So chi = 5 VERIFIED, a legitimate non-vacuous k=5 seed for the next block.
verified_results: GRADE [P] Monotonicity retraction, with proof. Forced equality does not carry upward in k; non-forcing does, since a separating k-colouring is a separating (k+1)-colouring. Lemma (proved): if G is (k-1)-colourable then no pair of distinct vertices is forced equal at k, because recolouring one endpoint with the unused k-th colour is proper and separates the pair. Consequence: a 4-colourable graph is provably incapable of a k=5 forced pair, so a k=5 seed must have chi >= 5.

GRADE [A] Construction, exact. tau=(3/2,sqrt3/2) verified |tau|^2 = 3 exactly in Q(sqrt3,sqrt5,sqrt11). U = induced unit-distance graph on V(H) union (V(H)+tau) with exact-coordinate dedup: 1106 points before, 1048 after, overlap 58 (A-only 495, B-only 495, shared 58). Total 5487 edges: 2722 internal to the A-copy, 2722 internal to the B-copy, and 184 NEW edges that lie in neither copy.

GRADE [A] chi(U) = 5, both bounds verified. Lower: the A-copy's internal edge count is exactly 2722 = |E(H)| with no extra A-internal edges, so H is an induced subgraph of U; H admits no proper 4-colouring (certificate certs/heule553_k4.drat, drat-trim verified), so U is not 4-colourable. Upper: an explicit proper 5-colouring of U, independently re-checked against all 5487 edges with 0 monochromatic, and its restriction to H has 0 monochromatic of 2722.

GRADE [A] Exactness and prefilter completeness. Every one of the 5487 edges was re-verified as an exact field identity with 0 failures. Floats nominated candidates only, in a band |d^2-1| < 1e-6; the max float error over the 2722 known unit edges is 7.77e-16; all 2722 known H-edges were recovered (0 missed); and of the rejected candidates the 400 closest to distance 1 were re-checked exactly with 0 unit pairs, the smallest |d^2-1| among rejected being 8.9e-5 (89x the band), so there is no borderline region.

GRADE [A] Structural verdict: the overlap is NOT a clique and there are 184 new cross edges, so Theorem A's clique-sum hypothesis fails on two independent counts. This is therefore a genuine non-clique-sum unit-distance union, as required for it to be capable of exceeding max(chi H, chi H) = 5 in principle.
GRADE [C] Inherited: the k>=5 no-forcing certificate on H (34 witnesses, 0 unseparated pairs), Theorems A/B/C, and the drat-trim-verified 4-UNSAT of H.
conjectures: U is a legitimate but not a promising k=5 forced-pair seed in one respect: U is 5-colourable and its 5-colourings may be numerous, which is the condition under which H had no forced pairs. Its interest is that adding the B-copy adds 184 new constraints on top of H, so forcedness can only increase relative to H; whether it does is the next measurement and is not decided here.

The 58-point overlap suggests tau=(3/2,sqrt3/2) is close to a symmetry of this particular point set. A translate with SMALLER overlap would create a more genuinely two-sided constraint structure; a translate with larger overlap approaches gluing a copy onto itself and risks reproducing H's freedom.

The two-percent density of new edges (184 new on 5487) is low. If the next block finds no forced pair on U, the productive direction is to choose tau from the lattice of vectors that maximise new-edge count, which is a cheap pre-computation over the finite set of tau realising distances already present in H's difference set.

escalation.obstacle: Find a genuine forced-equal distinct pair at k = 5, which by the corrected lemma requires a graph that is not 4-colourable. U = H union (H+tau) is such a graph (chi = 5, verified) and is the current seed; whether any of its 149906-equivalent non-adjacent pairs is forced has not been tested.
escalation.definitions: A unit-distance graph is a finite graph with an injection into R^2 such that uv is an edge iff |u-v| = 1. Proper k-colouring: c(u) != c(v) on every edge. A pair is forced equal at k if G is k-colourable and G plus the edge pq is not; the added edge is a combinatorial disequality constraint and, for a non-adjacent pair, never a unit edge. Coordinates in Q(sqrt3, sqrt5, sqrt11) with basis {1,3,5,11,15,33,55,165}.
escalation.hypotheses: Exact real-algebraic coordinates; complete finite induced unit-distance graph; k = 5; G must satisfy chi(G) >= 5 for the question to be non-vacuous.
escalation.attempted_approaches: Palette excluders via common neighbours (Theorem B: at most 2 colours excludable); clique-sum gluing (Theorem A: cannot raise chi); a complete k>=5 no-forcing certificate on H (34 witnesses); and now the exact non-clique-sum union U with chi = 5 verified, 58-point overlap and 184 new cross edges.
escalation.expected_useful_output: Either a forced-equal distinct pair in U at k=5, reported with exact coordinates, the separating-witness certificate or the proof certificate that justifies it, or a no-forcing certificate for U showing that 184 additional cross-unit edges still do not pin any pair. In the second case the informative next quantity is the mapping tau -> number of new cross edges, since the seed family should be indexed by constraint density rather than by overlap size.
